report.source_text: The patient received oral prednisolone at an initial dosage of 35 mg/day (1 mg/kg/day). This helped in rapid epithelialisation of the erosions on the back. The intraoral erosions diminished significantly in 2 weeks, and the dose was tapered to 30 mg/day. A marked improvement in the lesions was observed on subsequent follow-up. The patient is currently on prednisolone treatment (15 mg/day), and to date, no other lesions have been reported.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris (PV) with minimal skin lesions
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 90-year-old Japanese woman presented with a 3-month history of painful gingivae followed by a 3-week history of multiple painful erosions and easily ruptured vesicles on the buccal mucosa, palate, lateral tongue border, and gingiva, with difficulty eating. Physical examination revealed multiple erosions and desquamation with erythematous areas on the oral mucosa, positive Nikolsky's sign, and minimal skin involvement (few erythematous erosions on the back). Gingival biopsy histopathology demonstrated intraepithelial cleavage with acantholysis in the suprabasal region and retention of basal keratinocytes along the basement membrane zone. Serological testing by indirect immunofluorescence ELISA revealed elevated anti-desmoglein-3 (126 U/mL) and anti-desmoglein-1 (21 U/mL) antibodies. Direct immunofluorescence showed IgG and C3 deposition between epithelial cells. The patient was treated with oral prednisolone at an initial dose of 35 mg/day (1 mg/kg/day), which resulted in rapid epithelialization of back erosions and significant diminishment of intraoral erosions within 2 weeks. The dose was tapered to 30 mg/day with marked improvement on follow-up, and the patient is currently maintained on 15 mg/day prednisolone with no new lesions reported.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Clinical presentation of mucosal-dominant disease with minimal skin involvement
Histopathological confirmation of suprabasal intraepidermal acantholysis with basal cell retention
Elevated anti-desmoglein-3 and anti-desmoglein-1 antibodies by ELISA
Direct immunofluorescence showing intercellular IgG and C3 deposition
Rapid therapeutic response to corticosteroid treatment with epithelialization of lesions
